status_note: Closes the FLOAT-OPINT2FLOAT-SIGN-0001 residual of RULE-COLLAPSECONSTANTS-0001: Ghidra FloatFormat::opInt2Float sign-extends its integer input from sizein bytes (float.cc:611-617, sign_extend at address.hh:543) and opFloat2Float runs the bit-level convertEncoding ladder (float.cc:622-626 -> 352-419) — both driven directly on the public FloatFormat(4)/FloatFormat(8) constructors (the same IEEE 754 defaults Translate::getFloatFormat serves, translate.cc:966-971) with same-input/same-output bit patterns on both sides. 36 cases: negative INT2FLOAT at every input width (1/2/4/8 bytes) and both 4/8-byte targets, sign_extend's discard of bits above the sizein sign bit, INT32_MIN/INT32_MAX/2^24+1 and i64::MIN/MIN+1/MAX cast rounding (RNE is the oracle's overflow semantics), FLOAT2FLOAT widening/narrowing with negatives, negative zero, negative NaN (sign preserved), infinity, subnormal normalize, exact RNE ties and one-ULP-above-tie, denormalized output, underflow zero, and the DBL_MAX uintb wrap-carry overflow to infinity.

architecture.spaces: none; FloatFormat is constructed directly (public constructor) — no Architecture, Translate, or spec loading on either side

compiler_spec.prototype_xml: none; pure FloatFormat arithmetic with no Funcdata or calling convention

analysis_options.api: Direct production FloatFormat::opInt2Float(a, sizein) and opFloat2Float(a, outformat) calls on both sides; no PrintC, Action, or Rule pipeline (the rule integration is RULE-COLLAPSECONSTANTS-0001's covered projection)
analysis_options.formats: FloatFormat(4) and FloatFormat(8) constructed via the public default IEEE 754 settings constructor on both sides; identical to Translate::getFloatFormat defaults
analysis_options.normalization: None. Results are the full uintb/u64 return values printed as 0x%016llX; no ID, order, or state normalization
analysis_options.random_seed: none; pure functions over explicit bit patterns

input_manifest.canonicalization: SHA-256 of UTF-8 json.dumps(cases, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=False)

observation_schema.format: 37 fixed-order UTF-8 lines with final newline: one banner (schema=1|fixture=...|oracle=e40ed13...) then 36 `case=<id>|res=0x<16 uppercase hex>` records
observation_schema.projection: res is the complete uintb/u64 return value of the mapped function for the exact same input bits, input byte width, and output format on both sides

decisive_semantics.reference_output_parameters: Both functions are const pure methods returning uintb by value; opFloat2Float takes the output FloatFormat by reference and reads (never writes) it; convertEncoding reads formin fields via pointer. No shared state, no output parameters. Rugra mirrors with &self/&outformat reads and a u64 return.
decisive_semantics.loop_bounds_traversal_order: No loops in either function. opInt2Float is a straight line: sign_extend -> (double) cast -> getEncoding. convertEncoding branch order is decisive: NaN/Inf (exp==formin.maxexponent) -> subnormal normalize (exp==0) -> normal jbit room -> exp+=bias -> too-small (exp < -frac_size) -> denormalized (exp<1) -> roundToNearestEven -> overflow (exp>=maxexponent) -> pack. Rugra keeps the identical branch order.
decisive_semantics.counter_accumulator_lifecycle: exp is a signed int4 accumulator across the ladder (-bias-lz | -bias, then +bias, +1 only on round-carry); signif is a shift-state accumulator whose roundToNearestEven `+= midbitmask` relies on uintb wrap-around, detected by (signif>>63)==0 and rebalanced to 1<<63 with exp+=1 (float.cc:391/403). Rugra uses i32 exp arithmetic and wrapping_add on u64 signif with the same rebalance.
decisive_semantics.sorting_comparison_keys: No sorts. The decisive comparisons: sign_extend bit index 8*sizein-1 with shift amount 64-8*sizein (address.hh:543-549); roundToNearestEven predicate (signif&midbitmask)!=0 && ((signif&epsmask)!=0 || odd) with lowbitmask=1<<lowbitpos when lowbitpos<64 else 0 (float.cc:279-287); jbitimplied tested on the OUTPUT format (float.cc:379) not formin; oracle extractFractionalCode top-aligns the fraction (float.cc:113-119) and setFractionalCode consumes top-aligned codes (float.cc:144-153) — the convertEncoding ladder is written entirely in that convention.
